title: Analytics & UI Ops — Scrum Digest (2026-07-09)
content:
Quick scrum digest for the Console & Tooling cross-functional scrum (analytics + UI + rollout ops).

Date: 2026-07-09
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Marta, Jonas, Rafael, Sam (oncall), Lila (product PM) — a few joined asynchronously; notes below capture async updates.

High-level summary:
- Primary focus this sprint: stabilize analytics event ingestion (reducing dashboard lag spikes), unblock UI canary that failed on user-metadata queries, and land instrumentation for rollout feature-flag fidelity.
- Observed two regressions post-6/30 deploy: (1) attribution mismatch in per-route latency charts, (2) intermittent GraphQL 500s for /user-metadata during heavy canary traffic.
- Plan: small hotfix for GraphQL resolver (Jonas), rollout metric alignment patch (Ethan), and analytics backfill job + improved TTL handling (Marta).

Notes / conversation fragments (informal):
- Marta: "ingestion backlog last Thursday peaked at ~3h; memory pressure then triggered compaction that dropped a small batch of events — investigating retention window logic in ingestion-service v1.8.2"
- Jonas: "user-metadata GraphQL error traced to new DB connection pool behavior under sticky-circuit mode; changing pool size + timeout should help. I have a patch ready; will run local canary tomorrow."
- Ethan: "route attribution incorrectly attributing tokens to 'default' route for ~10% of samples — looks like an upstream header rename (x-redwood-route -> x-rd-route) from the gateway change. Quick fix on parser side, but need to reconcile historical metrics (backfill?)"
- Rafael: "UI screenshot diff tests failing because of font fallback variance on macOS agents — switching to deterministic text renderer in CI for the next run."
- Lila: asked for a short risk note for the team to send to customer-success (about possible dashboard gaps during the backfill). Draft included below.

Blockers (what's blocking progress):
- Access to the long-retention S3 bucket for the analytics backfill job is pending legal approval (ticket RED-2199). Marta cannot run backfill without that.
- Oncall capacity: Sam is handling a PSC incident today — may delay canary rehearse if follow-ups are needed.
- Font pipeline credential rotation caused some CI flakes (Rafael to follow up with infra).

Decisions made in-sync:
- Proceed with staged rollout for the GraphQL pool fix: dev -> canary(10%) -> full rollout. Canary will run against a small subset of internal users first.
- Attribution header migration: parser will accept both header names for 2 weeks, then switch to x-rd-route only. Backfill for affected metric windows will be queued after legal approves S3 access.
- Temporary dashboard badge: add "partial data" banner for affected charts until reconciliation completes.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Jonas: push PR to fix DB pool and open canary tomorrow A.M. (ETA: 2026-07-10). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/697
- Ethan: parser patch to accept legacy and new headers + small reconciliation script stub (ETA: 2026-07-11). Jira RED-2148 assigned.
- Marta: prepare backfill job plan and resource estimate; follow up on RED-2199 (legal). (ETA: backfill plan 2026-07-12).
- Rafael: pin deterministic text renderer in CI and restart failing screenshot runs (ETA: EOD 2026-07-09).
- Priya: draft customer-facing incident note (short) and share to #cs-ops for review (ETA: 2026-07-09 noon).
- Sam: if incident subsides, assist with canary observability checklists for Jonas (ETA: 2026-07-10).

Observability / telemetry deep-dive items to follow up:
- Add a per-request header sampling tag for route attribution so we can retroactively filter bad-attribution windows without reprocessing everything. (Ethan + infra)
- Expose canary-specific dashboards with side-by-side comparisons (latency, errors, user-metadata 500s) for the first 24h of rollout. (Marta + Priya)
- Add automated alert if ingestion backlog > 30m for more than 4 consecutive sampling intervals (currently it's set at 90m). (SRE team)

Unresolved questions / open threads:
- Should we run a conservative backfill (dedupe-by-id + time-window) or try a full reprocess? Tradeoffs: dedupe is fast but might miss correlated attribution corrections; full reprocess is heavy (compute cost + S3 egress). Need org input on cost budget for one-off corrections.
- Legal: any constraints on reprocessing user-identifiable event payloads from the long-retention bucket? (RED-2199). If yes, we may need to implement a PI-masking pre-stage.

Quick risk note (copy for CS/ops):
- Title: Short-term analytics fidelity impact during backfill
- Summary: A subset of dashboard charts that depend on route-header-based attribution may show incomplete data for windows between 2026-06-29 and 2026-07-02 due to header migration. We are scheduling a backfill; customers may notice missing datapoints and transient "partial data" badges. No user request payloads are being altered; backfill will only reconcile attribution keys.
- ETA for reconciliation: earliest 2026-07-15 (dependent on legal access approval).
- Contact: cs-ops@redwood.com, eng-console-tooling Slack channel.

Meeting followups / next syncs:
- Quick check-in tomorrow 2026-07-10 09:30-09:45 (15m): canary readiness + backlog status.
- Longer sync Wednesday 2026-07-13 11:00-12:00: deep-dive on backfill options + cost estimates (invite finance briefly).

Misc notes / scratchpad (items to copy into PRs / tickets):
- "parser: accept x-redwood-route and x-rd-route for 14d; emit deprecation warn in logs"
- "ingestion: if compaction drops events, emit retention-drop metric with samples tagged by region"
- "canary: compare user-metadata 200/500 ratio across both replica sets"

Closing thoughts (informal):
- Good cross-team alignment today; the set of small fixes should remove the visible customer pain quickly if we can unblock S3 access and Sam can free up for canary ops.
- Keep PRs small and labelled with jira ids so CS can link them into incident notes.

Attachments / links (for quick reference):
- Jira: RED-2148 (attribution parser), RED-2199 (S3 access/legal), RED-2201 (graphql pool patch)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/697
- Confluence: confluence:console-rollouts-canary-playbook-v2

-- end of digest.

Notes to self: move this digest into the weekly standup folder after finalizing edits; add a follow-up line in Friday's retro about "instrumentation debt" and scheduling an "observability hackday".
